themes_detail.label: Street disorder surge in Central Harlem
themes_detail.summary: Multiple indicators of street-level disorder are spiking this week across Central Harlem: litter basket requests up 1900% (5 complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average), illegal posting up 2300% (3 complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average), sidewalk condition complaints up 237% (16 complaints this week vs. 4.8 weekly average), and public drinking complaints up 1100% (3 complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average), suggesting a coordinated or environmental shift in neighborhood conditions.
evidence: Litter basket requests: 5 complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 10.97)
Illegal posting: 3 complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)
Sidewalk condition: 16 complaints this week vs. 4.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.3)
Public drinking: 3 complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35)
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: visit specific blocks with clustered complaints this week to document conditions and interview residents/business owners
Timeline investigation: did a specific event or policy change trigger this week's spike, or is this organic deterioration?
City response: contact Sanitation, Parks, and NYPD to understand what operational shifts (or failures) explain the sudden surge

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and encampments rise sharply
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped 833% to 7 complaints last week (vs. 0.8 weekly average, z-score: 4.81), and encampment complaints rose 279% to 18 complaints last week (vs. 4.8 weekly average, z-score: 3.92), suggesting a visible deterioration in public spaces and possible confluence with homelessness issues that the Community Board has flagged as a repeated budget priority.
evidence: Graffiti complaints: 7 last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.81, up 833%)
Encampment complaints: 18 last week vs. 4.8 weekly average (z-score: 3.92, up 279%)
Community Board has made 'upgrade existing facilities for the homeless' a recurring budget request, indicating chronic unmet need
reporting_angles: Map encampments and graffiti clusters last week to identify if concentrated in specific zones (e.g., transit hubs, parks) and interview affected residents
Interview DHS and Parks Department on resource allocation to Central Harlem vs. other districts in past 2-3 weeks
Profile individuals in encampments to understand what drove the sudden visible increase

themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise escalation
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints spiked 266% to 27 complaints this week compared to 7.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.5), a sharp divergence that suggests either a specific traffic or enforcement issue emerging this week in Central Harlem.
evidence: Vehicle noise complaints: 27 this week vs. 7.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.5, up 266%)
Spike isolated to this week only, suggesting acute trigger rather than chronic problem
reporting_angles: Identify which streets/avenues generated most vehicle noise complaints this week and visit them to observe conditions and interview residents
Check NYPD traffic enforcement data for major incidents, construction, or special events that week
Determine if street racing, delivery service congestion, or event-related traffic is the culprit

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped 1500% to 8 complaints 2 weeks ago compared to 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.5), indicating either increased street vending activity or sudden enforcement action that residents are reporting; timing aligns with broader street disorder spike.
evidence: Vendor enforcement complaints: 8 two weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.5, up 1500%)
Spike timing (2 weeks ago) precedes but may relate to this week's street disorder escalation
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors, local business owners, and residents on whether new enforcement sweeps or vendor activity changes occurred 2 weeks ago
Check NYPD and Department of Consumer Affairs enforcement logs for vendor-related activity in Central Harlem 2 weeks ago
Determine if vendor complaints reflect genuine public nuisance or enforcement friction
